$comment: Canonical st-gateway failure conditions and what a client service must answer for each. Source of truth for the conformance tests in agent-service, fleet-service and navigation-service, which vendor this file verbatim. See ../docs/design/upstream-errors.md.

cases.name: game-refusal
cases.why: SpaceTraders refused the action in this ship state. The gateway passes the game's status and body through unchanged.

cases.name: game-cooldown
cases.why: A 409 from the game. Distinguishable from a refusal only by status and code, which is why both are relayed.

expect.message: Ship action is still on cooldown.

cases.name: caller-unauthenticated
cases.why: The caller's own session was rejected. Collapsing this to 502 would tell the caller the fleet is broken when their token has simply expired.

cases.name: credential-not-configured
cases.why: auth-service has no agent token yet. An operator has to act; nothing retries its way out of it. The 503 and this exact sentence are the only signal that says so.

cases.name: auth-service-unavailable
cases.why: The same status as the case above, and a different problem: this one resolves on its own. Relaying the message is what keeps them apart.

gateway.body: {"error":{"message":"auth-service unavailable: cannot obtain a SpaceTraders credential"}}

expect.message: auth-service unavailable: cannot obtain a SpaceTraders credential

cases.name: spacetraders-unreachable
cases.why: The gateway reached its own limit of retries against the game. It is a 502 because the gateway says so, not because the client decided to make it one.

expect.message: SpaceTraders unreachable: dial tcp: i/o timeout

cases.name: body-too-large
cases.why: The gateway's own body-size limit. A 413 relayed as a 413 tells the caller to send less; relayed as a 502 tells them to try again, which will not help.

cases.name: non-envelope-error-body
cases.why: A proxy or load balancer between here and the gateway answering with HTML. There is no message to lift, so the raw body stands in, truncated.

cases.name: empty-error-body
cases.why: A non-2xx with nothing in it at all. Still relayed by status; the message is the client's own, since there is none to relay.

cases.name: gateway-unreachable
cases.why: No response at all: connection refused, DNS failure, read timeout, or a body that died mid-read. The only condition the client itself gets to classify, because the gateway never spoke.

cases.name: unusable-success-body
cases.why: A 2xx the client cannot use — not JSON, or missing the envelope the game always sends. The gateway answered and the client cannot pass it on, which is what 502 means.
